May 9, 2024

Overall good but has some flaws. The vegan leather barely breathes at all, leading to sweaty ears quite quickly. The noise cancelling is good in certain environments, but it's not that great at blocking out voices. Finally, the Bluetooth software stack is not ideal, as it's not fully compatible with all versions of bluez on Linux, but this is not too difficult to work around by installing an older version of bluez. This works well with other headphones, so the Fairbuds XL are certainly doing something a little bit out of spec.

Some minor notes:
- the lack of a 3.5 mm port is an odd omission. I don't think an adapter is a very nice workaround
- the battery remaining reported over the Bluetooth protocol and through the app do not match very well. This is quite confusing. In my phone's Bluetooth settings, it currently says 50% while the app claims 30%
- Doing a factory reset on the headphones doesn't actually reset the EQ profile, which is strange

May 6, 2024

When you buy these headphones, you are making a compromise. You sacrifice quality for fair wages of workers in the supply chain and ecological materials from which the headphones are made, and you gain a product that is easy to repair.
Unfortunately, according to my research, the headphones could have a manufacturing defect and are susceptible to breaking the headband base.
The ear cups could be a bit larger and versions with different materials could be available.
In addition, the fit of the elements could be better, e.g. the headband cover does not fit evenly on the headband.
Fairphone is a relatively new brand on the market and still suffers from "childhood problems". An example would be an insufficiently tested firmware update or a poorly selected repair centre (with a lot of bad reviews).

I'm a ridiculously heavy user of headphones. As well as regular use, I often sleep in then to cover the noise of a CPAP machine, as well as daytime use. My last three sets of major-brand headphones have all failed at the vertical-axis hinges.

These are very comfortable, and wearable for a long time. They don't interfere with sleep.

I've repeatedly worn them for entire days. The slight discomfort of not having a vertical-axis rotation of the ear cups is, I think, a very fair compromise.

The noise cancelling seems pretty well alongside my previous xm4's.

The battery life just blows my previous headphones out of the water. First time I've had a set realistically at >2 days and nights rather than 7-8 hours.

Feeling far more robust and solid than other headphones I've used, and the fact that it's repairable means it should massively outlast them.

I'm delighted.

Jun 29, 2023

I am higly disapointed, i knew i was buying the product for it's sustenability, but i was expecting it to be all around way better as i won't be using it.

First, it's not confortable, it get warm quickly and have barely any breathability.
The closed back design, unlike other, make it quite echoy, and any rubbing from your hair or head wear on the plastic will be quite noticeable.

The default noise floor is very hard to determine as the device minimal volume is crazy high. On my galaxy note 9 and my laptop the headset won't emit any sound under 9% of volume, like if it was on mute. Then it's immediately slightly higher than my normal confortable listening level.
That mean no podcast or calm music late at night for me. (Or with a jack, no volume issue with it, but then why buying this)

Sound quality, outside of the mecanical noise, is ok to me, i'm no audiophile.
The "sound profile" are very weird... city name, not very explicit and requiere the app to switch ... give user an EQ, not what ever this is.

Then ANC...
It's a feature on the box... but it's' quite the downgrade !
It does help a bit with whooshing sound like AC, but that's it, it does nothing for noise, talking, city noise like car... and it bring a very high and noticeable hiss or noize.
Sadly there are no way to have it disable all the time and it will be back on the next time you turn the headset on.

Mic isn't good from what other tell me but it could be a bluetooth generality as i am comming from a modmymic.

Finaly, i wanted to order a replacement battery at the same time as the headset to avoid another shipping co2 cost, but they don't have itnon their shop...

I will now have to debate betweend the carbon cost of returning it (will it be repackaged or go to the bin ?) Or having it stay in a box for ever...

Guillaume

Answer from Fairphone

Hello Guillaume, thanks very much for sharing these suggestions and bringing this to our attention. We’re so sorry to hear about your experience. We can see you are currently being assisted by our support team via e-mail. Best, Lorena

The Earphones look awesome and work well with the app and by using the controls on the ear patch. However, I had to send them back because I wasn't pleased at all with the modes for ambient sound (voice through) and active noise cancelling. Both modes are useless outside if there is only the slightest wind. I also tried them in office where I intended to use the noise cancelling for. There was still a lot of ambient sound coming through (keyboard clicks, collegues on telephone calls etc.). The "normal" headphone mode sounded good but I have the feeling that the price is way too high if you can only use them without the two other modes.
